questions.q: What is the primary function of the repeated phrase "tks gqvk gksxk" (whatever happens, happens) in the story? State its literal meaning and its thematic evolution in one sentence.
questions.a: The phrase begins as fd'kunk's fatalistic acceptance of life's hardships but transforms into a damning critique of the family's passive complicity in his neglect, exposing how "acceptance" becomes a tool of oppression when wielded by the powerful against the vulnerable. A wrong answer that only defines the phrase literally ("it means accepting fate") reveals the student is stuck at literal comprehension and misses the author's ironic deployment of the phrase across different speakers and contexts.

questions.q: Explain why the author chooses to narrate fd'kunk's death through the son's delayed discovery (the "Mh-vkbZ-tSM-" signboard, the construction site) rather than showing the death scene directly. What interpretive effect does this distance create?
questions.a: The narrative distance mirrors the emotional distance the son maintained during fd'kunk's life; by denying us the deathbed scene, the author forces the reader to experience the same hollow, bureaucratic aftermath the son faces — reducing a human life to a "signboard" and a construction site — thereby making the reader complicit in the dehumanization. A wrong answer focusing on "sparing the reader grief" or "pacing" misses the structural parallel between narrative form and thematic content.

questions.q: Apply the concept of "dramatic irony" to the scene where ;'kksèkj ckcw refuses to eat the "osQd" (leftover food) sent by his wife, claiming "vaMk iM+k gksrk gS" (it causes gas), while fd'kunk once fed him the same leftovers with love. What does this inversion reveal about the cyclical nature of care and neglect?
questions.a: The dramatic irony lies in the son rejecting the very sustenance he once survived on, unaware that his father's "foolish" generosity was the only reason he grew strong enough to now reject it. This inversion reveals that neglect is not a rupture but a continuation — the son weaponizes the same biological reality (digestion) that his father accommodated, turning care into transaction. A wrong answer that merely labels it "irony" without tracing the generational parallel fails to apply the concept to the story's core argument about cyclical karma.

questions.q: Analyze how the setting of the "DokVZj" (village/community space) functions as a character in the story. Compare its portrayal in fd'kunk's youth (communal feasts, shared grief) versus its portrayal at the end (construction sites, "Mh-vkbZ-tSM-" boards, strangers building "eaf”kyk"). What does this transformation diagnose about Indian modernity?
questions.a: The DokVZj shifts from a space of reciprocal ritual (shared meals, collective mourning) to a site of extraction (land sold for hospitals, strangers profiting from displacement), diagnosing modernity as the replacement of organic community with institutional transaction. The "eaf”kyk" (hospital) built on fd'kunk's land literally concretizes how care has been outsourced to impersonal systems. A wrong answer that describes the setting changes without linking them to the theme of "legkm baçkij" (blind faith in progress) treats setting as backdrop rather than active commentary.

questions.q: Evaluate the daughter-in-law's (iRuh) final act of feeding the "osQd" to the laborers instead of her husband. Is this an act of rebellion, pragmatism, or complicity? Defend your judgment using three textual details.
questions.a: It is pragmatic complicity: she redirects waste to those who "need" it (laborers), maintaining household economy without challenging the power structure — evidenced by (1) her immediate compliance when the son asserts authority ("yksx pys x,] bldk eryc ;g FkksM+h gS"), (2) her earlier participation in the "xSl" (ritual) she privately doubts, and (3) her focus on "fizQt" (utility) over sentiment. A wrong answer calling it "rebellion" ignores her ultimate submission to the son's "legkm baçkij" logic; calling it "pure pragmatism" ignores her silent resentment ("fp<+rh").

The monologue must reference the "DokVZj", his "ckck" (father), and the "Mh-vkbZ-tSM-" board.
questions.a: Sample: "tks gqvk gksxk — DokVZj bech diya, ckck ki yaad bech di, aaj Mh-vkbZ-tSM- board par apna naam dekh kar samjha: main nahi, meri zameen jeeti hai."
